mcq.q: A transducer:
o: Converts energy or physical quantities from one form to another at the boundary of the system
mcq.e: Sensors (input) and actuators (output).

mcq.q: Which is a digital sensor?
mcq.e: It gives two discrete states (closed or open).

mcq.q: A reed switch:
o: Is normally open and closes in a magnetic field
mcq.e: Detects presence of magnetic energy.

mcq.q: The AH1815 is a(n):
o: Omnipolar Hall-effect switch with open-drain output
mcq.e: Output is pulled low when the field exceeds the operating point (either pole).

mcq.q: The open-drain output of a Hall switch needs:
o: A pull-up resistor (the internal pull-up can be used)
mcq.e: Otherwise the pin floats when the output is off.

mcq.q: PIR stands for:
mcq.e: It detects variation of IR radiation in its field of view.

mcq.q: The ADXL335 accelerometer gives:
mcq.e: Needs three ADC channels.

mcq.q: A thumb joystick provides:
mcq.e: Two potentiometers.

mcq.q: A sound sensor module gives:
o: Both an analog voltage and a threshold digital output
mcq.e: Analog/digital sensor.

mcq.q: Actuators:
o: Convert electrical energy into other forms to change the physical world
mcq.e: Motors, solenoids, lamps, heaters, relays.

mcq.q: Why can't a DC motor be driven directly from an I/O pin?
o: It needs more current than the pin can supply
mcq.e: Pins supply only about 20 mA.

mcq.q: The purpose of a flyback diode across a motor or relay coil is to:
o: Absorb the voltage spike when the inductive load is switched off
mcq.e: It gives the collapsing coil current a safe path.

mcq.q: A flyback diode is connected with its cathode to:
o: The +V supply side of the coil
mcq.e: Reverse biased in normal operation.

mcq.q: In a BJT switch the base resistor:
o: Limits the base current taken from the pin

mcq.q: To saturate a BJT switching 100 mA you supply a base current of about:
mcq.e: Rule of thumb: I_B ≈ I_C / 10.

mcq.q: The correct base resistor for I_B = 10 mA from a 5 V pin (V_BE = 0.7 V):
A MOSFET differs from a BJT because it is controlled by:
mcq.e: The gate is insulated.

mcq.q: Why add a 10 kΩ resistor from the MOSFET gate to GND?
o: To keep it off while the pin floats
mcq.e: Defines the gate level during reset or programming.

mcq.q: The 2N7000 can switch up to about:
mcq.e: 60 V and 200 mA continuous.

mcq.q: The BC547 is a:
mcq.e: BC547: NPN, 45 V, 100 mA.

mcq.q: Which load is best switched by a relay?
mcq.e: Isolated contacts. Only with qualified supervision.

mcq.q: The relay terminals COM and NO mean:
mcq.e: NO closes when the coil energises; NC opens.

mcq.q: When a motor and Arduino use separate supplies, you must:
mcq.e: The transistor needs a common reference.

mcq.q: In the Hall sensor code, magnet present with a pull-up gives PIND bit:
mcq.e: The open-drain output pulls the pin low.

mcq.q: What does PIR stand for (as the lecturer stressed)?
mcq.e: Pyroelectric InfraRed; 'passive infrared' is the common mistake he pointed out.

mcq.q: Why are reed switches used where flammable gases are present?
o: The contacts and any spark are sealed inside a glass tube with inert gas
mcq.e: An open switch's spark can ignite gas; the reed switch keeps it inside the sealed tube.

mcq.q: A PIR mounted facing the gate may miss an intruder because...
o: It only detects movement across its field of view, not straight towards it
mcq.e: Mount it so people cross in front of it.

mcq.q: Why use a Hall effect sensor rather than a reed switch for ABS wheel speed?
o: Solid state: faster switching, no wear, longer life
mcq.e: No mechanical contacts, so it is fast and durable; pulse rate gives RPM.

mcq.q: Compared with a BJT, a MOSFET is...
o: Voltage-driven, switches faster, runs cooler, but costs more
mcq.e: The gate takes a voltage, not a current; faster and cooler, more expensive.

mcq.q: A 5 V relay coil needs about 70 mA. How do you drive it from an ATmega328P pin?
o: Through a BC547 with a 1 kΩ base resistor and a 1N4001 flyback diode across the coil
mcq.e: The pin gives at most 40 mA; the coil is an inductor so it needs a flyback diode.

mcq.q: Which module output is normally LOW and goes HIGH on detection?
mcq.e: Gas (and PIR) go HIGH on detection; flame, sound and soil go LOW.

written.q: Classify sensors with two examples of each class and explain how each class is read by the microcontroller.
written.a: Digital sensors (reed switch, Hall effect switch, PIR, flame) give two discrete voltages and are read on a digital pin with PINx / digitalRead (pull-up for open-drain or switch types). Analog sensors (water level, accelerometer, joystick, LDR, LM35) give a continuous voltage and are read by the ADC. Analog/digital sensors (sound, soil moisture, gas/smoke modules) provide both a continuous voltage and a threshold output.

written.q: A 6 V DC motor (150 mA) must be switched on and off from a 5 V pin. Design the driver with a BC547 and justify the component values.
written.a: Pin → RB → base; emitter to GND (common with the Arduino); motor from the 6 V (or 9 V) supply to the collector; 1N4001 across the motor with the cathode to +V. Saturation needs IB ≈ 150/10 = 15 mA, RB = (5 − 0.7)/0.015 = 287 Ω, use 270 Ω; but the pin limit is about 20 mA, so a MOSFET (2N7000 has 200 mA limit and negligible gate current) is the better driver. The flyback diode absorbs the spike when the motor coil is switched off.

written.q: Explain how a relay allows a microcontroller to control a mains lamp, and the precautions needed.
written.a: The pin switches a transistor that energises the relay coil (flyback diode across the coil). The relay contacts (COM and NO) are a separate circuit in series with the lamp's live wire, so the mains is isolated from the microcontroller. Precautions: qualified supervision, rated contacts, fuse, insulated enclosure, correct isolation, no breadboard or exposed wiring for mains.

written.q: Compare BJT and MOSFET switches for a microcontroller load.
written.a: The BJT (BC547) is current controlled and needs a base resistor sized for IB ≈ IC/10; limit 100 mA. The MOSFET (2N7000) is voltage controlled, draws almost no gate current, switches faster (good for PWM), limit 200 mA; add a gate pull-down. Both need a flyback diode for inductive loads and a shared ground.

written.q: Explain how a BJT lets a microcontroller drive a 75 mA motor, and why a flyback diode is needed.
written.a: The pin (max 40 mA) drives a tiny base current through 1 kΩ into an NPN transistor; this allows a much larger collector–emitter current from a separate 9 V supply (common ground) to flow through the motor. When switched off, the spinning motor coil (self-induction) produces a reverse voltage spike that would destroy the transistor; a 1N4001 across the motor (cathode to +V) gives it a safe path.

written.q: Give two advantages and two disadvantages of thermoelectric (Peltier) coolers.
written.a: Advantages: no moving parts or compressed gas (reliable, long life, maintenance free); same device heats and cools. Disadvantages: high cost per unit of cooling; poor power efficiency (e.g. 12 V 5 A = 60 W for a 2×2 inch module).
